classification.difficultyReason: Construct a prism from specified cross-section properties and visualise assemblies into a hexagonal prism and a honeycomb.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Draw a prism with a cross-section that is a quadrilateral with two parallel sides of unequal length and the other two sides of equal length.

answer.short: A prism with an isosceles trapezium cross-section, as shown.
answer.worked: Draw an isosceles trapezium: its parallel sides have unequal lengths and its other two sides are equal. Draw an identical translated trapezium and join corresponding vertices to form the prism.

spec.description: Unfilled isosceles-trapezium prism. Corresponding vertices are joined; hidden edges are dashed.
spec.mathematics: The front cross-section has parallel bases of lengths 2 and 1 in illustrative coordinates and equal non-parallel sides. The second cross-section is an identical translation. These illustrative lengths are not additional question givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Entire drawing appears only in answer editions.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Show with a drawing how two of the prisms of part a may be put together to form a hexagonal prism.

answer.short: Join the prisms along the rectangular faces containing their longer parallel cross-section sides, as shown.
answer.worked: Place two congruent isosceles-trapezium cross-sections on opposite sides of their common longer base. Their outer boundary is a hexagon. Extend both cross-sections through the same prism length; the joined solid is a hexagonal prism. The middle line in the drawing marks the join.

spec.description: Hexagonal prism formed from two congruent trapezium prisms. A horizontal diameter across its front hexagon marks the shared rectangular face; hidden rear join and hidden edges are dashed.
spec.mathematics: The regular hexagonal cross-section splits along a diameter into two congruent isosceles trapeziums, matching the example chosen in part a.
spec.answerVisibility: Entire construction appears only in answer editions.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Show with a drawing how a number of prisms with cross-sections of a regular hexagon may be put together to form a ‘honeycomb’.

answer.short: Place equal-length regular hexagonal prisms side by side with adjoining rectangular faces, so their hexagonal ends form a honeycomb.
answer.worked: Arrange congruent regular hexagons edge to edge. Three hexagons meet at each interior vertex because $120^\circ+120^\circ+120^\circ=360^\circ$, leaving no gaps. Extend every hexagon through the same length in the same direction to obtain adjoining hexagonal prisms.

spec.description: Four adjoining regular hexagonal prism ends in a staggered honeycomb cluster, with equal parallel depth edges. Ordinary outlines are black; hidden edges are dashed.
spec.mathematics: Congruent regular hexagons share complete sides without gaps. All prisms extend through the same translation, so adjoining hexagons correspond to adjoining rectangular prism faces.
spec.answerVisibility: Entire honeycomb drawing appears only in answer editions.
